claim: Protein ubiquitination regulated by ubiquitin ligases plays important roles in innate immunity.
source: Protein ubiquitination regulated by ubiquitin ligases plays important roles in innate immunity.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Fbxo21 is a functionally unknown component of SCF (Skp1–Cul1–F-box protein) complex.
source: F-box only protein Fbxo21, a functionally unknown component of SCF (Skp1–Cul1–F-box protein) complex
evidence: The manuscript states that Fbxo21's function was unknown prior to this study.

claim: Fbxo21 facilitates Lys29-linkage of ASK1.
source: F-box only protein Fbxo21, a functionally unknown component of SCF (Skp1–Cul1–F-box protein) complex, facilitates Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1 (apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental data including ubiquitination assays shown in the figures.

claim: Fbxo21 promotes activation of ASK1.
source: F-box only protein Fbxo21, a functionally unknown component of SCF (Skp1–Cul1–F-box protein) complex, facilitates Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1 (apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1)
evidence: This is supported by kinase activity assays and phosphorylation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Fbxo21 promotes type I interferon production upon viral infection.
source: F-box only protein Fbxo21, a functionally unknown component of SCF (Skp1–Cul1–F-box protein) complex, facilitates Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1 (apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1), and promotes type I interferon production upon viral infection.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data showing IFNβ production in various experimental conditions.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage of ASK1.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1
evidence: This is demonstrated by ubiquitination assays in Fbxo21-/- cells shown in Figure 6.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced activation of ASK1.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1
evidence: This is supported by phosphorylation and kinase activity data in Fbxo21-/- cells.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) signaling pathway.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1, attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling pathway
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot analysis showing decreased JNK phosphorylation in Fbxo21-/- cells.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency attenuates p38 signaling pathway.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1, attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling pathway
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot analysis showing decreased p38 phosphorylation in Fbxo21-/- cells.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency decreases the production of proinflammatory cytokines upon viral infection.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1, attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling pathway, and decreases the production of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferon
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data showing decreased IL-6 production in Fbxo21-/- cells.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency decreases the production of type I interferon upon viral infection.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1, attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling pathway, and decreases the production of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferon
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data showing decreased IFNβ production in Fbxo21-/- cells.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency results in reduced antiviral innate response.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1, attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling pathway, and decreases the production of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferon, resulting in reduced antiviral innate response and enhanced virus replication.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing decreased cytokine production and increased virus replication.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency results in enhanced virus replication.
source: Fbxo21 deficiency in mice cells impairs virus-induced Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1, attenuates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 signaling pathway, and decreases the production of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferon, resulting in reduced antiviral innate response and enhanced virus replication.
evidence: This is demonstrated by plaque formation assays showing increased virus titers in Fbxo21-/- cells.

claim: Fbxo21 is required for ASK1 activation via Lys29-linkage of ASK1 during antiviral innate response.
source: Therefore Fbxo21 is required for ASK1 activation via Lys29-linkage of ASK1 during antiviral innate response
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The innate immune system serves as the first line defense of invading microorganisms and endogenous danger signals.
source: Innate immune system serves as the first line defense of invading microorganisms and endogenous danger signals.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge in immunology.

claim: Host cells can recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) of invading pathogens via pattern recognition receptors (PRRs).
source: Host cells can recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) of invading pathogens via pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), initiate signaling pathways to regulate the expression of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferons (IFN α/β) (Yin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yin et al., 2015.

claim: PRRs initiate signaling pathways to regulate the expression of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferons.
source: Host cells can recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) of invading pathogens via pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), initiate signaling pathways to regulate the expression of proinflammatory cytokines and type I interferons (IFN α/β) (Yin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yin et al., 2015.

claim: Upon virus infection, host cells can recognize viral components, especially nucleic acids derived from viral genome or produced during viral life cycle.
source: Upon virus infection, host cells can also recognize viral components, especially nucleic acids derived from viral genome or produced during viral life cycle (Gürtler and Bowie, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gürtler and Bowie, 2013.

claim: Viral RNAs are mainly detected by RIG-I-like receptors (such as RIG-I and MDA5).
source: Viral RNAs are mainly detected by RIG-I-like receptors (such as RIG-I and MDA5) that induce type I IFNs via MAVS (mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein, also known as IPS1, Cardif and VISA)–dependent activation of TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)–interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) signaling pathway (Chan and Gack, 2015; Yoneyama et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chan and Gack, 2015 and Yoneyama et al., 2015.

claim: RIG-I-like receptors induce type I IFNs via MAVS-dependent activation of TBK1-IRF3 signaling pathway.
source: Viral RNAs are mainly detected by RIG-I-like receptors (such as RIG-I and MDA5) that induce type I IFNs via MAVS (mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein, also known as IPS1, Cardif and VISA)–dependent activation of TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)–interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) signaling pathway (Chan and Gack, 2015; Yoneyama et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chan and Gack, 2015 and Yoneyama et al., 2015.

claim: Viral DNAs are detected by multiple DNA sensors that induce type I IFNs mainly via STING-dependent TBK1-IRF3 signaling pathway.
source: On the other hand, viral DNAs are detected by multiple DNA sensors that induce type I IFNs mainly via stimulator of interferon genes (STING, also known as MITA, MPYS and ERIS)–dependent TBK1–IRF3 signaling pathway (Paludan and Bowie, 2013; Cai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Paludan and Bowie, 2013 and Cai et al., 2014.

claim: Ubiquitin modification is one type of the crucial posttranslational modification mechanisms.
source: Ubiquitin (Ub) modification is one type of the crucial posttranslational modification mechanisms, and has been implicated in regulation of both innate and adaptive immunity (Jiang and Chen, 2011; Zinngrebe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang and Chen, 2011 and Zinngrebe et al., 2014.

claim: Ubiquitin modification has been implicated in regulation of both innate and adaptive immunity.
source: Ubiquitin (Ub) modification is one type of the crucial posttranslational modification mechanisms, and has been implicated in regulation of both innate and adaptive immunity (Jiang and Chen, 2011; Zinngrebe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang and Chen, 2011 and Zinngrebe et al., 2014.

claim: The Cullin-RING multisubunit ligase complexes are assembled on the cullin backbones.
source: As compared to the typical single subunit E3 ligases (such as RING-finger type and HECT type E3 ligases), the Cullin-RING multisubunit ligase complexes are assembled on the cullin backbones and have been implicated in diverse processes (Skaar et al., 2013; 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Skaar et al., 2013 and 2014.

claim: SCF complex is an example of the Cullin-RING multisubunit ligase complexes.
source: S phase kinase-associated protein 1 (Skp1)–cullin 1 (Cul1)–F-box protein (SCF) complex is example of the Cullin-RING multisubunit ligase complexes (Skaar et al., 2013; 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Skaar et al., 2013 and 2014.

claim: In SCF complex, Skp1 binds to F-box domain of many F-box proteins.
source: In this complex, Skp1 binds to F-box domain of many F-box proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SCF complex structure.

claim: More than sixty F-box proteins have been identified up to date.
source: More than sixty F-box proteins have been identified up to date, and they have been classified into three categories: those with WD40 domain (Fbxw), those with leucine-rich repeats (Fbxl) and those with other diverse domains (Fbxo) (Jin et al., 2004; Skaar et al., 2013; 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jin et al., 2004 and Skaar et al., 2013 and 2014.

claim: F-box proteins have been classified into three categories: those with WD40 domain (Fbxw), those with leucine-rich repeats (Fbxl) and those with other diverse domains (Fbxo).
source: More than sixty F-box proteins have been identified up to date, and they have been classified into three categories: those with WD40 domain (Fbxw), those with leucine-rich repeats (Fbxl) and those with other diverse domains (Fbxo) (Jin et al., 2004; Skaar et al., 2013; 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jin et al., 2004 and Skaar et al., 2013 and 2014.

claim: The function of SCF in immunity remains poorly understood.
source: Despite great achievements have been made for elucidating the roles of SCF complexes in cancer (Skaar et al., 2014), the function of SCF in immunity remains poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field at the time of the study.

claim: SCFFbxw1 (β-Trcp1) and SCFFbxw11 (β-Trcp2) complexes have been implicated in regulating NF-κB signaling by degrading IκBα or processing of p100 and p105.
source: Possibly the best characterized SCF complexes associated with immunity are the F-box– and WD40 repeat–containing Fbxw1 (also known as β-Trcp1, Fbw1a and Fwd1) and Fbxw11 (also known as β-TrCP2, Fbw11, Fbxw1b, Fbx1b and Hos) complexes that have been implicated in regulating NF-κB signaling by degrading IκBα or processing of p100 (also known as NFκB2) and p105 (also known as NFκB1) (Yaron et al., 1998; Shirane et al., 1999; Spencer et al., 1999; Tan et al., 1999; Wu and Ghosh, 1999; Orian et al., 2000; Fong and Sun, 2002; Lang et al., 2003; Amir et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: ASK1 (also known as Map3k5) is a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) kinase kinase that plays pivotal roles in stress and immune responses.
source: Apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1, also known as Map3k5) is a mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) kinase kinase that plays pivotal roles in stress and immune responses (Ichijo et al., 1997; Shiizaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ichijo et al., 1997 and Shiizaki et al., 2013.

claim: ASK1 can activate MKK4/6 and MKK3/7, leading to activation of JNK1/2 and p38 MAPKs.
source: ASK1 can activate MKK4/6 and MKK3/7, leading to activation of c-Jun N-terminal kinases (JNK1/2) and p38 MAPKs (Ichijo et al., 1997; Shiizaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ichijo et al., 1997 and Shiizaki et al., 2013.

claim: ASK1 is crucial for apoptosis in response to multiple stresses and factors.
source: ASK1 is crucial for apoptosis in response to multiple stresses and factors (Ichijo et al., 1997; Sagasti et al., 2001; Tobiume et al., 2001; Nishitoh et al., 2002; Maruoka et al., 2003; Takeda et al., 2004; Matsuzawa et al., 2005; Shiizaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: ASK1 has been implicated in Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-triggered innate responses.
source: ASK1 has also been implicated in Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-triggered innate responses (Matsuzawa et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Matsuzawa et al., 2005.

claim: ASK1 is a conserved protein expressed by many species ranging from C. elegans and drosophila to mammals.
source: Evolutionarily, ASK1 is a conserved protein expressed by many species ranging from C. elegans and drosophila to mammals (Ausubel, 2005; Irazoqui et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ausubel, 2005 and Irazoqui et al., 2010.

claim: ASK1 homologs in C. elegans (NSY-1) and drosophila (DASK1) are important in control of apoptosis or innate immunity.
source: ASK1 homologs in C. elegans (NSY-1) and drosophila (DASK1) are important in control of apoptosis or innate immunity (Ausubel, 2005; Irazoqui et al., 2010; Shiizaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ausubel, 2005, Irazoqui et al., 2010, and Shiizaki et al., 2013.

claim: Fbxo21 knockdown significantly inhibited the mRNA levels of Ifnb upon LPS or VSV treatments.
source: We found that Fbxo21 knockdown most significantly inhibited the mRNA levels of Ifnb upon LPS or VSV treatments (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Fbxo21 is abundantly expressed by multiple tissues and macrophages.
source: Moreover, we found that Fbxo21 is abundantly expressed by multiple tissues and macrophages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Upon LPS treatments, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ by PMs, BMMs and RAW264.7 cells was all significantly decreased after Fbxo21 knockdown.
source: We found that upon LPS treatments, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ by PMs, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs) and RAW264.7 cells was all significantly decreased
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Fbxo21 knockdown only minimally affected IL-6 and IFNβ production of macrophages treated with CpG-ODN and TLR3 agonist poly (I:C).
source: But Fbxo21 knockdown only minimally affected IL-6 and IFNβ production of macrophages treated with CpG-ODN (TLR9 agonist) and TLR3 agonist poly (I:C) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–F).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-F.

claim: Upon infection with VSV and HSV-1, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ was significantly impaired in macrophages after Fbxo21 knockdown.
source: Upon infection with VSV and HSV-1, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ was significantly impaired in macrophages after Fbxo21 knockdown (Figure 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells demonstrated significantly impaired IL-6 and IFNβ production in response to LPS treatment, transfection of poly (I:C), poly (dA:dT) and poly (dG:dC), or infection with VSV and HSV-1.
source: Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells demonstrated significantly impaired IL-6 and IFNβ production in response to LPS treatment, transfection of poly (I:C), poly (dA:dT) and poly (dG:dC), or infection with VSV and HSV-1 (Figure 2B–E).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2B-E.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency significantly promoted the replication of VSV and HSV-1 in RAW264.7 cells and L929 fibroblasts.
source: More importantly, Fbxo21 deficiency significantly promoted the replication of VSV and HSV-1 in RAW264.7 cells and L929 fibroblasts (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by plaque formation assay data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Fbxo21 dose-dependently increased the mRNA expression of Il6 and Ifnb induced by VSV and HSV-1.
source: We found that Fbxo21 dose-dependently increased the mRNA expression of Il6 and Ifnb induced by VSV and HSV-1 (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 3B-E.

claim: Fbxo21 overexpression promoted the transactivation of AP-1, IFNβ and IRF3 reporters, but not NF-κB reporter, upon VSV and HSV-1 infection.
source: Correspondingly, we found that Fbxo21 overexpression promoted the transactivation of AP-1, IFNβ and IRF3 reporters, but not NF-κB reporter, upon VSV and HSV-1 infection (Figure 3F–I).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3F-I.

claim: The nuclear levels of active DNA-bound c-fos and IRF3, but not p65, were significantly decreased in Fbxo21–/– cells.
source: As further evidence, the nuclear levels of active DNA-bound c-fos and IRF3, but not p65, were significantly decreased in Fbxo21–/– cells (Figure 3J–O).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data for DNA-bound transcription factors shown in Figure 3J-O.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency inhibited the phosphorylation of JNK1/2 and p38 but not ERK1/2 mitogen-activated protein kinases.
source: We found that Fbxo21 deficiency inhibited the phosphorylation of JNK1/2 and p38 but not ERK1/2 mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), the type I IFNs-associated IRF3, but not the NF-κB-associated IKKα/β-IκBα (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency inhibited the phosphorylation of IRF3 but not the NF-κB-associated IKKα/β-IκBα.
source: We found that Fbxo21 deficiency inhibited the phosphorylation of JNK1/2 and p38 but not ERK1/2 mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), the type I IFNs-associated IRF3, but not the NF-κB-associated IKKα/β-IκBα (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Fbxo21 interacts with ASK1 under resting state.
source: Using IP assays in RAW264.7 and L929 cells, we found that Fbxo21 did interact with ASK1 under resting state (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The interaction of Fbxo21-ASK1 was increased 0.5–2 hr after virus infection, and was then decreased 3–4 hr after virus infection.
source: We found that the interaction of Fbxo21-ASK1 was increased 0.5–2 hr after virus infection, and was then decreased 3–4 hr after virus infection (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ASK1 or ASK1 with only the N-terminal segment could be coimmunoprecipitated with Fbxo21.
source: After transfection of Fbxo21 with ASK1 (mutants) plasmids (Figure 5C) in HEK293 cells, we found that ASK1 or ASK1 with only the N-terminal segment could be coimmunoprecipitated with Fbxo21 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Full-length Fbxo21 or C-terminal segment of Fbxo21 could be coimmunoprecipitated with ASK1.
source: When ASK1 was cotransfected with Fbxo21 (mutants) (Figure 5E) in HEK293 cells, it was found that full-length Fbxo21 or C-terminal segment of Fbxo21 could be coimmunoprecipitated with ASK1 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: GST fusion proteins of Fbxo21 and Fbxo21 (466–628 aa) could pull down recombinant ASK1.
source: As further evidence, we performed GST pull-down assays and found that GST fusion proteins of Fbxo21 and Fbxo21 (466–628 aa) could pull down recombinant ASK1 (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1 could be coimmunoprecipitated with Fbxo21.
source: To validate that Fbxo21 is a component of the SCF complex, we examined the endogenous Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1 in Fbxo21 immune complexes, and found that Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1 could be coimmunoprecipitated with Fbxo21 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Fbxo21, but not Fbxo21 without F-box domain, could interact with Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1.
source: Then we cotransfected Fbxo21 with conserved SCF components (Skp1, Cul1 or Rbx1) in HEK293 cells. We found that Fbxo21, but not Fbxo21 without F-box domain, could interact with Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: ASK1 could be polyubiquitinated after VSV and HSV-1 infection, which was significantly impaired in Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells.
source: We found that ASK1 could be polyubiquitinated after VSV and HSV-1 infection, which was significantly impaired in Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The degradation of ASK1 in Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells was not affected.
source: However, we found that the degradation of ASK1 in Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells was not affected (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ub with only the intact Lys29 residue (K29O-Ub) could be linked to ASK1 by Fbxo21.
source: We then analyzed the Ub-modification type of ASK1 by SCFFbxo21. We found that Ub with only the intact Lys29 residue (K29O-Ub) could be linked to ASK1 by Fbxo21 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Fbxo21 could promote the linkage of K29O-Ub to ASK1 after virus infection in Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells reconstituted with Fbxo21.
source: In Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells reconstituted with Fbxo21, we found that Fbxo21 could promote the linkage of K29O-Ub to ASK1 after virus infection (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 was abrogated when cells were treated with MLN-4924.
source: When the cells were treated with MLN-4924, an inhibitor of NEDD8-activating enzyme that has been implicated in the assembly of SCF complex (Soucy et al., 2009), we found that Fbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 was abrogated (Figure 6D,E)
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6D,E and citation to Soucy et al., 2009.

claim: In the presence of recombinant GST-Fbxo21, ASK1 and Cul1-Rbx1-Skp1, as well as the NEDD8 conjugation system, ASK1 could be efficiently polyubiquitinated in vitro.
source: In the presence of recombinant GST-Fbxo21, ASK1 and Cul1-Rbx1-Skp1, as well as the NEDD8 conjugation system (neddylation), ASK1 could be efficiently polyubiquitinated; while in the presence of MLN-4924, the polyubiquitination of ASK1 was significantly inhibited (left panel, Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: 6xHis-Ub-K29O (with only Lys29 in Ub), but not 6xHis-Ub-K29R (with the Lys29 mutated into Arg in Ub), could be linked to ASK1 in vitro.
source: To confirm the Lys29-linkage of Ub chains to ASK1, we used 6xHis-Ub-K29O (with only Lys29 in Ub) and 6xHis-Ub-K29R (with the Lys29 mutated into Arg in Ub) in the in vitro assays, and found that the former, but not the later, could be linked to ASK1 (right panel, Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The K13 mutant of ASK1 (mutation of Lys946, Lys950, Lys951, Lys952, Lys953 and Lys957 into Arg) could most significantly decrease the levels of polyubiquitinated ASK1.
source: We found that the K13 mutant of ASK1 (K13-ASK1; mutation of Lys946, Lys950, Lys951, Lys952, Lys953 and Lys957 into Arg) could most significantly decrease the levels of polyubiquitinated ASK1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B and Figure 7A.

claim: Wild type ASK1 but not K13-ASK1 could be polyubiquitinated in Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells reconstituted with Fbxo21 and infected with VSV or HSV-1.
source: In Fbxo21-/- RAW264.7 cells reconstituted with Fbxo21 and infected with VSV or HSV-1, we found that wild type ASK1 but not K13-ASK1 could be polyubiquitinated (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: K13-ASK1 demonstrated remarkably lower activity as compared to wild type ASK1.
source: Meanwhile, we found that K13-ASK1 demonstrated remarkably lower activity as compared to wild type ASK1 (Figure 7C, D).
evidence: This is supported by kinase activity assay data shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: The phosphorylation and activity of ASK1 were significantly impaired in both Fbxo21-/- cells and MLN-4924-treated cells after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
source: We found that the phosphorylation and activity of ASK1 were significantly impaired in both Fbxo21-/- cells and MLN-4924-treated cells after VSV or HSV-1 infection (Figure 7—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and kinase activity assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Fbxo21 deficiency significantly decreased the poly-Ub levels of ASK1.
source: We found that Fbxo21 deficiency significantly decreased the poly-Ub levels of ASK1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The K48- and K63-linked poly-Ub levels of ASK1 were not significantly affected by Fbxo21 deficiency.
source: However, the K48- and K63-linked poly-Ub levels of ASK1 were not significantly affected.
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The phosphorylation of ASK1 as well as the kinase activity of ASK1 both occurred later than poly-Ub modification of ASK1.
source: Moreover, the phosphorylation of ASK1 as well as the kinase activity of ASK1 both occurred later than poly-Ub modification of ASK1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is supported by time-course data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3C.

claim: In Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ triggered by VSV and HSV-1 infection was significantly inhibited.
source: In Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ triggered by VSV and HSV-1 infection was significantly inhibited while the virus titers of VSV and HSV-1 were significantly increased (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 8B,C.

claim: The virus titers of VSV and HSV-1 were significantly increased in Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells.
source: In Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells, the production of IL-6 and IFNβ triggered by VSV and HSV-1 infection was significantly inhibited while the virus titers of VSV and HSV-1 were significantly increased (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This is supported by plaque formation assay data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The activation of JNK1/2, p38 and IRF3 was significantly impaired in Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells infected with VSV and HSV-1.
source: Meanwhile, we found that the activation of JNK1/2, p38 and IRF3 was significantly impaired in Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells infected with VSV and HSV-1 (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: ASK1, but not K13-ASK1 or ASK1-K716A, could rescue the impaired IL-6 and IFNβ production and the inhibited antiviral response in Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells.
source: When the Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells were rescued by overexpression of ASK1, K13-ASK1 or ASK1-K716A (Lys716 mutated into Ala, kinase activity inactive), we found that ASK1, but not K13-ASK1 or ASK1-K716A, could rescue the impaired IL-6 and IFNβ production and the inhibited antiviral response (Figure 8A–D).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA and plaque formation assay data shown in Figure 8B-D.

claim: K13-ASK1 could not rescue the impairment in activation of JNK1/2, p38 and IRF3, phosphorylation on Thr845 of ASK1, and the kinase activity of ASK1.
source: Furthermore, we found that K13-ASK1 could not rescue the impairment in activation of JNK1/2, p38 and IRF3, phosphorylation on Thr845 of ASK1, and the kinase activity of ASK1 (Figure 8F,G).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and kinase activity assay data shown in Figure 8F,G.

claim: JNK1/2 inhibitor SP600125 significantly reversed Fbxo21-mediated activation of IRF3 after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
source: We found that JNK1/2 inhibitor SP600125 significantly, and pan-p38 inhibitor SB203580 to a much lesser extent, reversed Fbxo21-mediated activation of IRF3 (Figure 9A,B)
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 9A,B.

claim: Pan-p38 inhibitor SB203580 to a much lesser extent reversed Fbxo21-mediated activation of IRF3 after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
source: We found that JNK1/2 inhibitor SP600125 significantly, and pan-p38 inhibitor SB203580 to a much lesser extent, reversed Fbxo21-mediated activation of IRF3 (Figure 9A,B)
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 9A,B.

claim: JNK1/2 inhibitor SP600125 significantly reversed Fbxo21-mediated production of IL-6 and IFNβ after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
source: We found that JNK1/2 inhibitor SP600125 significantly, and pan-p38 inhibitor SB203580 to a much lesser extent, reversed Fbxo21-mediated activation of IRF3 (Figure 9A,B) and the production of IL-6 and IFNβ (Figure 9C,D) after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 9C,D.

claim: Pan-p38 inhibitor SB203580 to a much lesser extent reversed Fbxo21-mediated production of IL-6 and IFNβ after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
source: We found that JNK1/2 inhibitor SP600125 significantly, and pan-p38 inhibitor SB203580 to a much lesser extent, reversed Fbxo21-mediated activation of IRF3 (Figure 9A,B) and the production of IL-6 and IFNβ (Figure 9C,D) after VSV or HSV-1 infection.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 9C,D.

claim: ASK1 activation facilitated by SCFFbxo21 ubiquitin ligase complex plays an important role in promoting virus-triggered innate response.
source: Our study shows that ASK1 activation facilitated by SCFFbxo21 ubiquitin ligase complex plays an important role in promoting virus-triggered innate response, serving as a critical module in antiviral innate response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: SCF complexes may not only mediate degradation of protein substrates but non-proteolytic regulation of substrates.
source: More importantly, our study reveals a new type of Ub-modification (Lys29-linkage) in regulating kinase activation, and suggests that SCF complexes may not only mediate degradation of protein substrates but non-proteolytic regulation of substrates.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the finding that Fbxo21-mediated ubiquitination of ASK1 does not lead to degradation.

claim: ASK1 is a remarkably conserved kinase crucial in defense of infection.
source: Considering that ASK1 is a remarkably conserved kinase crucial in defense of infection (Ausubel, 2005; Irazoqui et al., 2010), our study may be of great significance for understanding of innate response in species other than mammals.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ausubel, 2005 and Irazoqui et al., 2010.

claim: E3 ligases, such as cIAP-1, SOCS1, zinc-finger protein A20 and Stub1 (also known as CHIP), have been implicated in degradation of ASK1.
source: E3 ligases, such as cIAP-1, SOCS1, zinc-finger protein A20 and Stub1 (also known as CHIP), have been implicated in degradation of ASK1 and thus a negative regulator of JNK and/or p38 activation and apoptosis (Zhao et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2009; Won et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhao et al., 2007, Yu et al., 2009, Zhang et al., 2009, and Won et al., 2010.

claim: The seven lysine residues of Ub (lys6, lys11, lys27, lys29, Lys33, lys48 and Lys63) can all be transferred to protein substrates by the ubiquitin system.
source: Ideally, the seven lysine residues of Ub (lys6, lys11, lys27, lys29, Lys33, lys48 and Lys63) can all be transferred to protein substrates by the ubiquitin system.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ubiquitin biochemistry.

claim: K33-linkage of CD3ζ promotes its phosphorylation and interaction with Zap70 and possibly the transport of CD3ζ to lysosomes for degradation.
source: Similar to the effects of Lys63-linkage, Lys33-linkage of CD3ζ promotes its phosphorylation and interaction with Zap70 and possibly the transport of CD3ζ to lysosomes for degradation (Ouchida et al., 2008; Huang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ouchida et al., 2008 and Huang et al., 2010.

claim: K33-linkage of Zap70 by Nrdp1 promoted the dephosphorylation of Zap70 and thus terminated early TCR signaling in CD8+ T cells.
source: Recently our study revealed that K33-linkage of Zap70 by Nrdp1 promoted the dephosphorylation of Zap70 and thus terminated early TCR signaling in CD8+ T cells (Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2015.

claim: TRAF6 has been implicated in Lys29-linkage but aggregation of huntingtin protein.
source: TRAF6 has been implicated in Lys29-linkage but aggregation of huntingtin protein (Zucchelli et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zucchelli et al., 2011.

claim: The E3 ligase Itch may mediate Lys29-linked polyubiquitination and degradation of Notch.
source: The E3 ligase Itch may mediate Lys29-linked polyubiquitination and degradation of Notch (Chastagner et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chastagner et al., 2008.

claim: Deubiquitinating enzyme USP9X is implicated in the removal of Lys29-linked ubiquitin from AMPK-related kinases.
source: Previously deubiquitinating enzyme USP9X is implicated in the removal of Lys29-linked ubiquitin from AMPK-related kinases (Al-Hakim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Al-Hakim et al., 2008.

claim: USP9X stabilizes ASK1 by removal of Ub chains from ASK1 and prevention of ASK1 degradation.
source: Meanwhile, USP9X stabilizes ASK1 by removal of Ub chains from ASK1 and prevention of ASK1 degradation (Nagai et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nagai et al., 2009.

claim: In Map3k5−/− MEFs, TNFα-induced apoptosis and JNK activation are attenuated.
source: In Map3k5−/− MEFs, TNFα-induced apoptosis and JNK activation are attenuated (Tobiume et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tobiume et al., 2001.

claim: In Map3k5−/− thymocytes, FasL-induced activation of JNK and p38 is decreased while the apoptosis of thymocytes is not significantly affected.
source: In Map3k5−/− thymocytes, FasL-induced activation of JNK and p38 is decreased while the apoptosis of thymocytes is not significantly affected (Tobiume et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tobiume et al., 2001.

claim: The primary neurons derived from Map3k5−/− mice are resistant to polyglutamine-induced cell death.
source: The primary neurons derived from Map3k5−/− mice are resistant to polyglutamine-induced cell death (Nishitoh et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nishitoh et al., 2002.

claim: Map3k5−/− mice demonstrate increased resistance to TLR4, but not TLR3 and TLR9, engagement, accompanied by impaired p38 activation.
source: More importantly, Map3k5−/− mice demonstrate increased resistance to TLR4, but not TLR3 and TLR9, engagement, accompanied by impaired p38 activation (Matsuzawa et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Matsuzawa et al., 2005.

claim: Upon infection with influenza virus, Map3k5−/− MEFs show decreased JNK and p38 activation and inhibited cell death.
source: Upon infection with influenza virus, Map3k5−/− MEFs show decreased JNK and p38 activation and inhibited cell death (Maruoka et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maruoka et al., 2003.

claim: ASK1 is usually activated via autophosphorylation after TRAF2− and TRAF6−assisted homodimerization in TNFα response.
source: It has been proposed that ASK1 is usually activated via autophosphorylation after TRAF2− and TRAF6−assisted homodimerization in TNFα response (Tobiume et al., 2002; Noguchi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tobiume et al., 2002 and Noguchi et al., 2005.

claim: JNK1/2 may be involved in activating IRF3 by phosphorylating IRF3 on Ser173.
source: Previously it has been reported that JNK1/2 may be involved in activating IRF3 by phosphorylating IRF3 on Ser173 (Zhang et al., 2009) or licensing TBK1-mediated IRF3 phosphorylation on Ser396 (Nociari et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2009.

claim: JNK1/2 may be involved in licensing TBK1-mediated IRF3 phosphorylation on Ser396.
source: Previously it has been reported that JNK1/2 may be involved in activating IRF3 by phosphorylating IRF3 on Ser173 (Zhang et al., 2009) or licensing TBK1-mediated IRF3 phosphorylation on Ser396 (Nociari et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nociari et al., 2009.

claim: Fbxo21 mRNA was induced by HSV-1 infection but decreased by VSV infection.
source: By using Q-PCR assays, we confirmed that Fbxo21 mRNA was induced by HSV-1 infection but decreased by VSV infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In the presence of Act D, the amounts of Fbxo21 protein were decreased after VSV and HSV-1 infection.
source: In the presence of Act D, the amounts of Fbxo21 protein were decreased after VSV and HSV-1 infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), indicating that Fbxo21 itself may be regulated by proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Fbxo21 itself may be regulated by proteasomal degradation.
source: In the presence of Act D, the amounts of Fbxo21 protein were decreased after VSV and HSV-1 infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), indicating that Fbxo21 itself may be regulated by proteasomal degradation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing decreased Fbxo21 protein in the presence of transcription inhibitor.

claim: In the presence of MG132, VSV infection could not decrease Fbxo21 while HSV-1 infection could induce the expression of Fbxo21 protein 12 hr after infection.
source: In the presence of MG132 that blocks the degradation of Fbxo21, we found that VSV infection could not decrease Fbxo21 while HSV-1 infection could induce the expression of Fbxo21 protein 12 hr after infection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Fbxo21 may act at an early stage of antiviral response while at a later stage the transcriptional regulation of Fbxo21 mRNA may contribute to the differences in innate response to RNA virus versus DNA virus.
source: Given that Fbxo21 was abundantly expressed in many cell types, it may be inferred that Fbxo21 may act at an early stage of antiviral response while at a later stage the transcriptional regulation of Fbxo21 mRNA may contribute to the differences in innate response to RNA virus versus DNA virus.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential regulation of Fbxo21 by VSV and HSV-1.

claim: The C-terminal part of Fbxo21 that contains one coiled-coil domain and one YccV-like protein domain may interact with the N-terminal part of ASK1 that contains one coiled-coil domain and one thioredoxin-binding domain.
source: These data suggest that the C-terminal part of Fbxo21 that contains one coiled-coil domain and one YccV-like protein domain, may interact with the N-terminal part of ASK1 that contains one coiled-coil domain and one thioredoxin-binding domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the domain mapping experiments shown in Figures 5D-G.

claim: Fbxo21 could form a complex with Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1 (SCFFbxo21).
source: These data indicate that Fbxo21 could form a complex with Skp1, Cul1 and Rbx1 (SCFFbxo21).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: SCFFbxo21 may mediate non-proteolytic polyubiquitination of ASK1.
source: These data indicate that SCFFbxo21 may mediate non-proteolytic polyubiquitination of ASK1.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that ASK1 is ubiquitinated but not degraded in the presence of Fbxo21.

claim: Fbxo21, by joining with Skp1-Cul1-Rbx1 (SCFFbxo21), is required for Lys29-linkage of ASK1.
source: These data suggest that Fbxo21, by joining with Skp1-Cul1-Rbx1 (SCFFbxo21), is required for Lys29-linkage of ASK1.
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitination assay data showing that Fbxo21 promotes K29O-Ub linkage to ASK1.

claim: SCFFbxo21 could promote the Lys29-linkage of ASK1 in vitro.
source: These data further validate that SCFFbxo21 could promote the Lys29-linkage of ASK1.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The K13 mutant-covered region in ASK1 may be the major ubiquitination sites modified by Fbxo21 during virus infection.
source: These data suggest that the K13 mutant-covered region in ASK1 may be the major ubiquitination sites modified by Fbxo21 during virus infection, and Fbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 may be required for ASK1 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that K13-ASK1 has significantly reduced ubiquitination and activity.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 may be required for ASK1 activation.
source: These data suggest that the K13 mutant-covered region in ASK1 may be the major ubiquitination sites modified by Fbxo21 during virus infection, and Fbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 may be required for ASK1 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that K13-ASK1 has significantly reduced activity.

claim: SCFFbxo21 is crucial for the phosphorylation and kinase activity of ASK1.
source: These data suggest that SCFFbxo21 is crucial for the phosphorylation and kinase activity of ASK1.
evidence: This is supported by data showing impaired ASK1 phosphorylation and activity in Fbxo21-/- cells and MLN-4924-treated cells.

claim: SCFFbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 may prejudge the activation of ASK1.
source: These data together indicate that SCFFbxo21-mediated Lys29-linkage of ASK1 may prejudge the activation of ASK1.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal relationship showing ubiquitination occurs before phosphorylation and activation.

claim: Lys29-linkage of ASK1 is required for ASK1 activation and the subsequent innate antiviral responses.
source: These data convincingly demonstrate that Lys29-linkage of ASK1 is required for ASK1 activation and the subsequent innate antiviral responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiments showing that K13-ASK1 cannot restore antiviral responses.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated antiviral innate response may mainly require ASK1-dependent activation of JNK1/2 and, to a lesser extent, p38.
source: These data suggest that Fbxo21-mediated antiviral innate response may mainly require ASK1-dependent activation of JNK1/2 and, to a lesser extent, p38 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the inhibitor experiments showing differential effects of JNK and p38 inhibitors.

claim: ASK1 activation facilitated by SCFFbxo21 ubiquitin ligase complex serves as a critical module in antiviral innate response.
source: Our study shows that ASK1 activation facilitated by SCFFbxo21 ubiquitin ligase complex plays an important role in promoting virus-triggered innate response, serving as a critical module in antiviral innate response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SCF complexes may exert functions via non-proteolytic modification of substrates.
source: Since most of SCF complexes mediate degradation of substrates (Skaar et al., 2013; 2014), our finding of SCFFbxo21-mediated non-proteolytic polyubiquitination of ASK1 may indicate that SCF complexes may exert functions via non-proteolytic modification of substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that Fbxo21-mediated ubiquitination does not lead to ASK1 degradation, which is novel for SCF complexes.

claim: Lys29-linkage of ASK1 could facilitate its phosphorylation and activation.
source: Our study suggests that SCFFbxo21 may be the ligase responsible for Lys29-linkage of ASK1 by demonstrating that Fbxo21 is required for Lys29-linkage of ASK1 upon viral infection, leading to non-proteolytic modification of ASK1 and ASK1 phosphorylation. Our data also indicate that Lys29-linkage of ASK1 could facilitate its phosphorylation and activation, and a crosstalk may exist between phosphorylation and Lys29-linked polyubiquitination.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that K13-ASK1 (which cannot be ubiquitinated) has reduced phosphorylation and activity.

claim: A crosstalk may exist between phosphorylation and Lys29-linked polyubiquitination of ASK1.
source: Our data also indicate that Lys29-linkage of ASK1 could facilitate its phosphorylation and activation, and a crosstalk may exist between phosphorylation and Lys29-linked polyubiquitination.
evidence: This is speculated based on the temporal and functional relationship between ubiquitination and phosphorylation.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated ASK1 activation is important in induction of type I IFN production upon VSV and HSV-1 infection.
source: Despite these convincing results, roles of ASK1 in innate antiviral response are not fully elucidated. Our study suggests that ASK1 activation by SCFFbxo21 is important in induction of type I IFN production, by using VSV and HSV-1 viruses as infection models.
evidence: This is supported by data showing decreased IFNβ production in Fbxo21-/- and Map3k5-/- cells.

claim: ASK1-mediated JNK activation, and to a lesser extent p38, is indispensable for type I IFN production.
source: Our study also suggests that ASK1-mediated JNK activation, and to a lesser extent p38, is indispensable for type I IFN production, which is similar to the previous reports investigating TNFα-death receptor interaction (Tobiume et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by inhibitor experiments and citation to Tobiume et al., 2001.

claim: Activity of ASK1 is regulated by many molecules that complex with ASK1 (ASK1 signalosome, about 1,500–2,000 kDa), such as ASK1 itself, ASK1 homologues, thioredoxin, TRAF2, TRAF6 and Daxx etc.
source: Activity of ASK1 is regulated by many molecules that complex with ASK1 (ASK1 signalosome, about 1,500–2,000 kDa), such as ASK1 itself, ASK1 homologues, thioredoxin, TRAF2, TRAF6 and Daxx etc. (Shiizaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shiizaki et al., 2013.

claim: SCFFbxo21 associates with ASK1 signalosome, adding new components to ASK1 signalosome.
source: In our study, we have found a complex containing Fbxo21 and SCF components, thus adding new components to ASK1 signalosome.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that Fbxo21 interacts with ASK1 and forms a complex with SCF components.

claim: ASK1 is required for type I IFN production during antiviral innate response.
source: When we are preparing the manuscript, it is reported that ASK1 is required for type I IFN production during antiviral innate response (Okazaki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okazaki et al., 2015.

claim: ASK1 deficient in Lys29-linkage could not rescue antiviral innate response in Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells.
source: More importantly, we found that ASK1 deficient in Lys29-linkage could not rescue antiviral innate response in Map3k5−/− RAW264.7 cells.
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments showing that K13-ASK1 cannot restore cytokine production and antiviral responses.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated Ub-modification and activation of ASK1 are essential for innate antiviral response.
source: Therefore, Fbxo21-mediated Ub-modification and activation of ASK1 are essential for innate antiviral response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comprehensive experimental data showing the requirement of Fbxo21 for ASK1 ubiquitination, activation, and antiviral responses.

claim: JNK1/2 may be involved in activating IRF3, which may explain the effects of JNK1/2 inhibition on decreased innate antiviral response mediated by Fbxo21.
source: Previously it has been reported that JNK1/2 may be involved in activating IRF3 by phosphorylating IRF3 on Ser173 (Zhang et al., 2009) or licensing TBK1-mediated IRF3 phosphorylation on Ser396 (Nociari et al., 2009), which may explain the effects of JNK1/2 inhibition on decreased innate antiviral response mediated by Fbxo21.
evidence: This is inferred from previous studies and the current data showing JNK inhibitor effects.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated ASK1 activation may be involved in regulation of antiviral innate response via JNK-dependent IRF3 activation.
source: Therefore, it can be inferred that Fbxo21-mediated ASK1 activation may be involved in regulation of antiviral innate response via JNK-dependent IRF3 activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that JNK inhibitor reduces IRF3 activation and cytokine production.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated regulation of ASK1 polyubiquitination and ASK1 activation may represent a new type of Ub modification by SCF complex.
source: In sum, our study has shown that Fbxo21 plays an indispensable role in regulating innate antiviral response by promoting the Lys29-linkage and activation of ASK1 and subsequently ASK1-mediated JNK1/2 activation. Therefore Fbxo21-mediated regulation of ASK1 polyubiquitination and ASK1 activation may represent a new type of Ub modification by SCF complex and act as an intrinsic part of antiviral innate response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the novel finding of non-proteolytic Lys29-linkage by SCF complex.

claim: Fbxo21-mediated regulation of ASK1 acts as an intrinsic part of antiviral innate response.
source: Therefore Fbxo21-mediated regulation of ASK1 polyubiquitination and ASK1 activation may represent a new type of Ub modification by SCF complex and act as an intrinsic part of antiviral innate response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comprehensive data showing the importance of Fbxo21-ASK1 axis in antiviral responses.
